items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: I struck up a friendship with Art Tatum

ctx.x: And also, that was one of the best moves I ever made because I struck up a friendship with Art Tatum, because even though Art was only playing five o'clock in the afternoon, and a half hour a day on the radio, he loved to play -- he could play for 12 hours a day, and every night after I finished with Milt, I'd get together with Art, and we'd go to the after hour places, and different peoples homes, and friends of ours who had a piano, and the two of us, and visiting pianists would play until oh, nine o'clock in…

Tatum was a tremendous influence on me as a jazz pianist, because back in school, I had had the recordings of Earl Hines and the early Fats Waller solos, 'A Handful Of Keys' -- Fats Waller was doing the solos for Victor in the late twenties, and Earl Hines had begun to record with Louis Armstrong and the Hot Five. 'West End Blues', and all those things he did at that time.
